paper.title_en: Pulsed to continuous-wave quantum dot cavity-QED
paper.abstract_en: Resonant cavity-quantum system interactions are well understood in the pulsed coherent and continuous-wave steady-state limits, but not much in between. We investigate the intermediate regime, where pulse duration, coupling, decoherences, and decays occur on comparable timescales, and pulse bandwidth matches cavity splitting and detunings. We reveal an interplay of cavity-enhanced excitation and Purcell-enhanced emission leading to warped chevron patterns. We develop a quantum master-equation model that efficiently treats the excitation-light coherent states in photon number space and reproduces the experimental data. Using these results we identify how polarization-split cavities can optimize single-photon purity and emission probability.
